card.name: Word meanings after foreign-language terms
card.fires_on: The word 'meaning', 'means' or 'for' (also a comma or quote) right after a foreign or root word, introducing its translation or etymology. Seen in word-origin explanations.

modes.label: Etymology gloss
modes.description: 'meaning' or 'means' after a Greek or other root word, giving its translation.
modes.example: Definition of Amylo- Amylo-: (Amyl- before a vowel.) A prefix pertaining to starch. From the Greek amylon,<< meaning>> starch.

modes.label: Place or name translation
modes.description: 'means' after a foreign name such as a Tibetan mountain, explaining what it translates to.
modes.example: The mountain sits on both sides of the border of Nepal and Tibet, about 30 km. west of Mount Everest. Cho Oyu in Tibetan<< means>> "the turquoise goddess ."

modes.label: Punctuation before gloss
modes.description: A comma or closing quote after a foreign term, just before its meaning is given.

card.writes: Little clear effect; the promoted tokens are mixed, loosely naming or describing people and things.
card.plain: It fires where a text is about to translate a foreign word, as in 'from the Greek X, meaning...'.

In Tibetan, ‘Pumo’<< means>> girl and ‘Ri’, mountain.
